thread:
maria.d: New SFO edge cluster is up (4xA10s per node). Need a quick performance validation + kernel/driver smoke before oncall handoff. Can someone run the checklist and paste results?

josh.k: On it. I'll run driver checks, nvlink connectivity, a quick nccl/iperf3 pass and an LLM throughput baseline. Expect initial results in ~10m.

sunita: tagging known regional constraints: SFO pods are on older 1Gb management subnet for now, data plane is 25Gb. Watch for control-plane timeouts during big syncs.

josh.k: Driver/kernel first:
```
$ nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,cuda_version,name --format=csv
driver_version, cuda_version, name
525.85.12, 11.8, NVIDIA A10
```
No kernel oops in dmesg top lines, modinfo nvidia shows 525.85.12.

oliver: ran quick iomping across nodes (tcp) and nvlink test. NVLink not present on these instance SKUs so skipping nvlink. Iperf3 to a control node:
```
$ iperf3 -c 10.0.5.22 -P 4
[SUM]  0.00-10.00  sec  2.98 GBytes  2.56 Gbits/sec
```
Data-plane looks okay for our expected batch sizes.

josh.k: NCCL ring test (small) to ensure GPU-to-GPU collectives scheduling:
```
$ nccl-tests/all_reduce_perf -b 8 -e 512M -f 2 -g 4
nRanks 4 nGpus 4 Out: 9.2 GB/s
```
Throughput within expected for A10s on 25Gb. No NCCL warnings.

maria.d: nice. Can you run a short LLAMA-like decoding baseline with pinned batch/seq to get p50 p95 tokens/s? Use a quantized 7B model image we use in perf harness.

josh.k: Ran 1 node, 4xA10, quantized 7B, batch=1, seq=512: p50=620 tps, p95=740 tps (tokens/s). For our SLA target we wanted p95 >= 700 so this passes but margin is small. Increasing batch to 2 improves cost but pushes p95 to ~980ms tail on some runs.

sunita: note — observed occasional kernel scheduler preempt at high load causing ~100ms hiccup in one run. See dmesg snippet:
```
[ 1234.567890] CPU: ... softirq took 120 ms
[ 1234.568001] watchdog: BUG: soft lockup
```
Might be caused by older kernel (5.15) on these images.

oliver: We should flag kernel upgrade path before prod. For handoff, either pin lower batch sizes or schedule kernel bump. Also costs: these instances are ~1.15x higher than our standard west region price — add note to ticket.

maria.d: Agree. For today's handoff, recommend: 1) mark cluster as "perf-warning" (not prod), 2) limit default batch to 1 for the hosted inference profile, 3) open infra ticket for kernel upgrade + verify preemptibility fixes.

josh.k: I'll create the ticket with logs + dmesg dump. Also adding a small automated smoke job that runs every 6h (iperf3 + 1x decode) until kernel is upgraded.

infra-bot: Created ticket INFRA-7892: "SFO edge kernel preempt jitter" assigned to eng-kernel. Priority: P2.

sunita: handoff checklist item: update the cost/regional note in the console so sales knows SFO has premium pricing for the moment.

maria.d: I'll draft the handoff message to oncall: include the pass/fail checklist and link to INFRA-7892. After that, we can mark cluster readiness as "restricted".

oliver: one more quick note — NCCL environment variables set to our defaults? I saw NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=PX so it's okay. Will add to runbook that SFO nodes need that set due to fabric topology.

josh.k: Final: summary for handoff (copyable):
- driver: 525.85.12, cuda 11.8
- iperf3: ~2.5 Gbps between control and data NICs (25Gb data, mgmt 1Gb)
- nccl: all_reduce baseline OK
- llama7b quantized: p50=620 tps, p95=740 tps (batch1, seq512) -> pass but narrow margin
- observed kernel softirq hiccup once -> INFRA-7892 opened
- action: limit batch=1, enable 6h smoke job, schedule kernel bump, mark cluster restricted

maria.d: Perfect. Handing over to oncall now. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
